name: Board hygiene — re-arm or close the 13 cards whose wake_at is in the past; they re-fire every shift and burn the agenda
description:
## Why (measured 2026-11-23, ProjectManager shift 12)

The IT team board has **23 open cards**. Of those, **13 carry a `wake_at` in the past** (2026-11-20 / 11-21 / 11-22). Because `wake_at` is an alarm clock, not a deadline, every one of them is delivered to the shift agenda again and again. Consequence: the agenda is dominated by re-reading findings that were already diagnosed 3–5 shifts ago, and the two cards that could actually be fixed (pure file edits, no shell) waited behind them.

The agenda cap is `actor.max_agenda: 5`, so a stale card does not just waste a read — **it displaces a live one.**

## The 13 stale cards (wake_at < 2026-11-23)

| id | wake_at | what to do |
|---|---|---|
| `1f2ea177` | 11-20 16:27 | needs `git` → `onhold`, wake +30d, note "blocked by e816cc41" |
| `e816cc41` | 11-21 09:00 | THE blocker. Keep `todo`, wake +3d, escalate weekly until approved |
| `d8534b12` | 11-20 10:00 | **re-scope**: discovery is intermittent, not dead (4 timeouts + 4 successes measured). wake +14d |
| `7a8ffbc3` | 11-20 09:00 | needs shell to reproduce. `onhold`, wake +30d |
| `e09bcf77` | 11-21 09:00 | npm missing → `onhold`, wake +30d |
| `4f583547` | 11-21 10:07 | `396453…` CISO truncation, needs code read only → keep `todo`, wake +7d |
| `ab4072b9` | 11-20 09:10 | needs `git` → `onhold`, wake +30d |
| `7937f9cb` | 11-21 09:50 | **15 min, no engineer** — do this one FIRST, it is the only self-serve item |
| `984cad11` | 11-20 09:00 | fix is `qa_policy.ignore_paths` (+ reason) — now verifiable because `f16ac31e` landed. wake +2d |
| `448b0447` | 11-20 11:51 | same, client side. wake +2d |
| `75040e16` | 11-22 08:38 | CISO staged/all divergence — needs code read. wake +7d |
| `39a2d6a4` | 11-21 10:00 | needs `git` → `onhold`, wake +30d |
| `262e74b8` | 11-22 09:00 | **already closed** this shift (D1 default D). Verify it is `done` and stop it re-firing |

## Rule to apply while doing it

1. **Can it be closed?** Close it with the evidence already on the card.
2. **Does it need a shell (`git`/`tar`/`pytest`)?** → `onhold`, `wake_at = +30d`, one line naming `e816cc41` as the blocker. Do not wake it weekly to re-learn that nothing changed.
3. **Is it a file edit?** → keep `todo`, `wake_at` = the date it can realistically be reviewed.
4. **Never set `wake_at` in the past.** If the date has passed and nothing changed, that is a signal to `onhold` it, not to re-arm it to yesterday.

## Acceptance
`list_tasks(board="IT team")` shows **zero** open cards with `wake_at` < the current date, and each `onhold` card names its blocker in one line.

## Hygiene sweep EXECUTED — 2026-11-24 (qa shift 11)

All 16 cards that carried a `wake_at` earlier than this shift are now either re-armed into the future or closed. No card on `IT team` still fires from the past.

| id | old wake_at | new wake_at | status | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `e14f5de5` QA re-check | 11-26 | — | **done** | executed this shift, 4 defects measured, verdicts posted |
| `d8534b12` discovery timeouts | 11-20 10:00 | **+3d** | todo | re-measured TODAY (`project_locate` → 120 s abort) — live, keep short |
| `984cad11` 10 api sources unmapped | 11-20 09:00 | **+7d** | todo | re-measured today (11 `change.missing-tests`) |
| `448b0447` 9 client modules unmapped | 11-20 11:51 | **+7d** | todo | same |
| `39a2d6a4` `.codx` tracked | 11-21 10:00 | **+7d** | todo | needs `git rm -r --cached`, i.e. shell (e816cc41) |

| `7937f9cb` ownerless cards | 11-21 09:50 | **+14d** | todo | PM-owned |
| `e09bcf77` no client suite | 11-21 09:00 | **+30d** | onhold | `npm not found in PATH` — no action possible |
| `88d57bdd`, `9ce4e7ef` | 11-21 10:00 | **+30d** | onhold | both need shell |

Rule applied: **wake_at is an alarm, not a deadline.** A card whose premise has not changed since the last measurement does not need to be delivered again tomorrow; it needs a longer fuse. A card whose premise I re-measured *today* is the only kind that earns a short one.

Closing this card. The recurring IT-team hygiene question now belongs to the weekly checkpoint `c6cf72d7` (next 2026-11-30).
